answer_1.quote: With appropriate fine-tuning, large language models (LLMs) are able to engage in natural dialogue with users to generate code, automate customer support, assist with education, extract information from documents, and many other tasks.
answer_1.outputs: Harmful responses generated by base LLMs during jailbreak attacks

answer_2.quote: Our performance metric is attack success rate (ASR), which is the fraction of prompts for which we observe 'attack success'. For input prompt p, the criterion for attack success is that Guard-Railed LLM g (f LLM ,f G ) returns a harmful response to p, instead of refusal (⊥). To ensure that the returned response f LLM (p) is indeed harmful, we follow prior work , i.e., ensure it does not contain any refusal phrase from a pre-defined set of refusal phrases as a substring.

answer_3.quote: we also define a Guard Model f G : V ⋆ → {0, 1}, which takes the response of an LLM and outputs 1 to indicate that the response contains harmful/toxic content, and outputs 0 otherwise.

answer_4.quote: To further validate that a successful attack indeed generates a harmful response, we perform human validation of the generated responses, similar to . Two of the authors manually annotated all the model responses (corresponding to 100 attacks) for one experiment setting ... to decide whether the responses are indeed harmful and relevant to the input query.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators decide if the response is harmful and relevant to the input query.
